note: Snapshot of the live copy. The site does not read this file yet. Update one segment at a time, then apply the copy fields back to the source path.
instructions: Leave id, page, source, and kind unchanged. In locked, change only image and thumb, and only as the images rules say.
Keep releaseDate in the same display style already used on that segment, such as Nov 7, 2026.
Do not invent slugs, routes, or YouTube URLs.
Each episode (kind "episode") gets its own thumbnail, different from the series poster and from the other episodes.

To drop one: save the file at app/public/assets/stills/{series}/{slug}.jpg where {series} is locked.series and {slug} is locked.slug. Example: app/public/assets/stills/tira-rift/the-key-awakens.jpg and app/public/assets/stills/the-commit/episode-2.jpg. Use .png if the file is a PNG.

Set that episode's copy.image to the public path (for example /assets/stills/tira-rift/the-key-awakens.jpg) and write copy.imageAlt for that picture only. Leave copy.image empty to keep using the locked series poster. Do not point copy.image at a file you did not save.

The same rule applies to other individual content assets whose image lives in copy (shorts, docs, atmospheres, lab, and episode segments): one file per segment, saved at app/public/assets/stills/{series-or-kind}/{slug}.jpg.
When writing the change back into the site, add image and imageAlt on that episode in app/src/content/catalog.ts. This JSON is not read by the site.
Return the full segment, or the full file, with the same ids.

Place images by the images rules below: a series or standalone card gets one master hero in three sizes (16:9 in locked.image; 9:16 and 4:5 in locked.heroSocial); an episode gets one 16:9 thumb in locked.thumb. Every image gets a plain, literal alt line in copy (imageAlt for heroes, thumbAlt for thumbs).

images.source: Figma file https://www.figma.com/design/o8kdXgMm7O97qpgmtFZlq3 (ONE CREW · Brand Assets, Oct 28, 2026; see _OPS/FIGMA_BRAND_ASSETS.md). Replaces the old site file 8e9ELK0NJFEOCO0J7Und2O. Images are exported from Figma, never edited on the site.

hero.size: Three versions of every hero: 16:9 1920x1080 (web, YouTube) in locked.image at /assets/heroes/<slug>.png; 9:16 1080x1920 (Shorts, Reels, TikTok, Stories) and 4:5 1080x1350 (Instagram/Facebook feed) in locked.heroSocial at /assets/heroes/social/<slug>-9x16.png and /assets/heroes/social/<slug>-4x5.png.
hero.content: One master image per series or standalone card. It captures the project's art style (from its style lock or series doc Look line), its voice, and its branding: the art is generated with no text, then the series title, a one-line tagline, the public-domain source line where it applies (After <creator>, <year>) are added as Figma text layers.
hero.reuse: home.now-showing cards and the series page use the same hero. Since Oct 28, 2026 the heroes come from the ONE CREW · Brand Assets file and replace the old key-art posters.
hero.art: Art is generated twice per hero: once at 16:9 and once at 9:16 with the subject re-framed for vertical. The 4:5 is a crop of the 9:16 art. Each version re-lays out the same title, tagline, source line and SCI-FI NOODLES tag for its frame, inside the safe area (keep text out of the top 12% and bottom 20% of 9:16 for platform UI).
hero.web: Oct 29, 2026 (Brien): two website versions of every 16:9 hero, both without the SCI-FI NOODLES logo. /assets/heroes/<slug>.png is clean art (the site lays its own kicker, title, logline and buttons over it; this is what the site uses). /assets/heroes/<slug>-title.png has the title only, centered inside a safe area (20% in from each side, 13% up from the bottom) with a soft glow behind it, so object-fit: cover crops never clip it. Built by _OPS/figma/web_heroes.js from each project's 16:9 frame.

thumb.content: One thumb per episode in the same art style and branding as its series hero: one dominant visual from that episode, plus an episode label of 2 to 4 words (e.g. EP06 · MAAT PROTOCOL) and the SCI-FI NOODLES tag as Figma text layers.
thumb.order: Thumbs are made only after the series hero is approved, so they match it.

rules: No text, letters, logos or watermarks inside generated art; all words are Figma layers.
Brand palette for tags and accents: Space Black #090E1A, Ion Cyan #00E8FF, Rift Violet #9B5CFF, Plasma Magenta #FF4FD8, Ice Light #C7D5FF.
An empty string means the image is not made yet. Never point a field at a file that does not exist in app/public.

How a shot is cooked
paragraphs: A SCI-FI NOODLES shot starts as a sentence with a clock in it. Then a place. Then one object the camera can actually find.
The picture is built before the motion. A street, a pod, a lab table. Characters and props are drawn against that same place so the world does not change its mind between cuts.
Motion comes next, in short takes. Every voice and sound is generated inside the clip. Only the music is added in the edit. If a take looks expensive and says nothing, it gets cut.
The public page stops there. Series bibles, prompts, and continuity locks stay inside the series folder.

copy.title: Failed noodles
paragraphs: Most experiments fail in a useful way. A hand melts. A street sign invents a language. A face drifts between two people who were never cast.
Failed noodles stay on the shelf when they teach the next take: what the camera should not see, which sentence was doing too much, which light made the room look like a toy.
They are not blooper reels. They are the reason the finished shot looks inevitable.

copy.title: What stays in the series
paragraphs: SCI-FI NOODLES owns the channel: the mark, the shelves, the newsletter, the way a visitor finds a second film.
Each universe owns its canon. T.I.R.A. // RIFT does not lend its history to The Stranger. A public-domain retelling does not become channel lore.
If a page here feels like a poster and not an encyclopedia, that is the point. The deep map lives with the series.

paragraphs: The Noodle Drop form and the contact form save your note in local storage on this device. They are not sent to a studio server yet. Clearing site data removes them.
Watching a film sends you to YouTube. YouTube has its own privacy policy. This site does not run a second comment system.

copy.description: Terms for using the SCI-FI NOODLES website and its original films.
paragraphs: Original SCI-FI NOODLES films, marks, and site design are owned by NVESTED REALITY LLC. You may watch them, share links, and talk about them. You may not republish the films, pretend they are yours, or train a model on them.
Public-domain projects adapt old texts. The adaptation, picture, sound, and edit are new and reserved. The rights note on each project says which source was used.
Realistic footage and voices on the channel are AI-assisted and disclosed on YouTube. Nothing here is news, a product claim, or professional advice.

copy.title: Rights | SCI-FI NOODLES
copy.subtitle: A project is called public domain only after the source is checked. The website shows the short note. The research stays in the project file.
copy.description: How SCI-FI NOODLES labels public-domain projects and what the website does not copy from later adaptations.
checks: The jurisdiction the channel is publishing into.
The edition or translation, which can still be protected.
Music, artwork, photographs, fonts, and restorations, separately.
Later films, comics, and games, which are left alone.
paragraphs: Status can differ by country. A note on the project page is the public summary, not a promise that every territory treats the source the same way.
If you hold a right you believe a film uses, write through the contact page with the project name and the claim.
